claims.text: add_members has no existence check before adding a user, so re-adding an existing group member hits the unique index on group_users and raises an unhandled 500 instead of a friendly error, and this is easy to trigger because the frontend never clears the input after submit.
Hardcoded colors #333 and #aaa in SCSS instead of SCSS variables may break theme consistency
Stray closing tag with no matching opening tag in group/members.hbs template

offset = params[:offset].to_i can produce negative offsets and limit can be <= 0, which may raise or produce invalid queries in ActiveRecord - need to clamp/sanitize limit and offset before calling .limit(...).offset(...)
usernames input is not cleared after add operation, making it easy to accidentally re-add the same usernames

The public members.json response format was changed in place from a plain array to an object (breaking change) with no expand/migrate/contract path, risking breakage for any third-party script or integration already consuming the old shape.
The same endpoint's offset parameter has no lower-bound check, so a negative offset value causes PostgreSQL to raise an error, resulting in an unhandled 500.

Both add_members and remove_member call params.require(:group_id), but the routes put the group's ID in params[:id], not params[:group_id], causing ActionController::ParameterMissing for every real HTTP request

The public group members page is now silently truncated to 50 entries (previously unlimited for non-automatic groups) with no pagination UI at all, so visitors have no way to see or even know about members beyond the first 50.

Item-view template references `member`, but that alias is not available inside a separate `itemView` template. The row will render with missing member data, and clicking remove can throw when the controller calls `member.get(...)`.

Several unrelated pure-formatting changes (ilike to ILIKE plus blank line, indentation of private/protected sections, a full reorder of an .hbs file, blank-line removal in another .hbs) are mixed into this behavioral commit, making the diff hard to review.

remove_member bypasses the Group model and calls group.users.delete directly, skipping the cleanup that used to null out primary_group_id, so a removed member's posts continue to display flair for a group they no longer belong to.

add_members writes members one at a time in a loop with no transaction, so when one username in a batch fails (e.g. duplicate), earlier usernames in the same batch are already committed, leaving the group in a partially-applied state.

findMembers now returns undefined on its early-return path instead of a resolved promise like before, making its return type inconsistent between code paths even though no current caller chains .then on it yet.

Two lines have misleading semicolon placement (a lone semicolon after a block that looks like part of the return statement, and a missing semicolon relying on ASI) that make the reader stop to double-check.
A previously-existing test coverage for 'silently skip adding non-existent usernames' was removed with no equivalent replacement, even though that behavior is preserved in the new code.
There is no test coverage at all for the new response format's meta.total/limit/offset fields that the frontend depends on.
Does moving a block of shared form-styling CSS rules under .groups, .badges risk breaking styling on other pages that also relied on the original shared container?
PUT is used for the non-idempotent add-members action, violating PUT's replace-the-resource semantics; the same request body sent twice produces different results (success, then a 500 from F-001).
Guard condition in group/members.hbs checks model but loop iterates over members - if model is truthy but members is undefined/empty, table header renders with no rows

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.

Stray closing tag inside a with no matching opening
, which is invalid HTML and may cause browser rendering issues
Usernames are not normalized before lookup in add_members - whitespace or blank entries will silently skip valid users

The public /groups/:name/members.json endpoint passes an unvalidated limit parameter straight into SQL with no upper bound, and since it's anonymously reachable and trust_level_0 includes every user on the site, any anonymous visitor can dump the entire site's username/name/avatar/last_seen list in one request (also enabling large-result-set DoS).

A '// TODO: should clear the input' comment shipped as-is, meaning the username input isn't cleared after a successful add, which is the direct trigger for the duplicate-add 500 (F-001) since users naturally click Add again.
HTTP method mismatch in .remove_member - test uses PUT but remove_member action expects DELETE

remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) which performs a direct SQL DELETE bypassing ActiveRecord callbacks including counter_cache, causing group.user_count to become stale after member removal. Should use group.remove(User.find(user_id)) instead which properly triggers counter cache updates.

The automatic variable may not be in scope for the item view template - if it resolves against the member context it may be undefined, causing the remove control to show even for automatic groups, which would allow clicking remove and likely surface a 422 without UI handling
Pagination params limit and offset are not clamped - negative or very large values can trigger heavy queries or odd behavior
The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
After group.users.delete(user_id), is the groups.user_count counter cache still accurate, given Rails' has_many :through #delete may not trigger the destroy callbacks that maintain the counter?
A pending pagination test that is exactly what this MR is supposed to fix was never enabled, and its assertions still assume the old array response shape rather than the new {members, meta} format.
Route parameter mismatch - routes provide :id but controller expects :group_id, causing param is missing error
